Important points regarding CPR;

⇨Reversible cause – survival is more
⇨Non pregnant – laryngeal airway or supraglottic airway are acceptable but not in pregnant it is not suitable due to risk of regurgitation, mucosal bleeding and further intubation is difficulty due to blood and obscured view.
⇨Abdominal USG by expert to look for concealed hemorrhage.
⇨Vasovagal & epilepsy => commonest cause of collapse.
⇨Manual uterine displacement or left lateral tilt
⇨Perimortem C/S
362.If >20 weeks
363.Aim for uterine evacuation within 5 min
364.No response despite correct performance of CPR within 4 min
365.Achieved within 5 min
366.69% infant survival
367.Hypoxic brain damage of neonate if perimortem C/S performed after 6min.

 

⇨Cardiac arrest 50% survival of mother.

54% survived until discharge

42% with mod – good Neurological outcomes.

⇨More favorable outcome when CPR performed within 10min.

Identification of impending Collapse:

368.Obstetric MEW score chart – all women under observation to allow early recognition.
369.Miss unwell women

Causes of collapse and their management (4T,4H):

⇨VTE – most common cause of maternal death
⇨Haemorrhage 6/1000, among most common causes of direct maternal death.
⇨AF embolism
-1.7/100,000, Mortality 67/1000
-Presents during labour, birth or within 30 min of birth.
-Collapse, Hypotension, Respiratory distress, Hypoxia.
-Coagulopathy if mother survives, due to complement activation.

Treatment:

370.Supportive treatment after Resuscitation
371.Involvement of obstetrician, haematologist, Anesthetist, intensivist (Senior)
372.Early aggressive treatment of coagulopathy including FFP
373.rFVII used if coagulopathy not corrected with massive blood component replacement.
374.rFVII – associated with poor outcome
⇨Cardiac Disease:
375.Most common cause of indirect death
376.1/5th dies during transfer in ambulance/ ER.
377.Majority of deaths has no previous history
378.Main causes of death are arrythmia and ischemia with structurally normal heart

Ehler Danlos: inter scapular pain, wider pulse pressure due to systolic HTN, cardiac murmur.

 

 

Treatment:

379.After resuscitation – Expert cardiologist evaluation
380.Thrombolysis => cause placental size bleeding but should be given with acute coronary insufficiency.

381.Percutaneous angioplasty – safe in pregnancy
⇨Drug Toxicity/ Overdose:

Mgso4;

10ml of 10% ca Gluconate is given when toxicity is suspected

Local Anesthetics:

-Due to high plasma concentration of local anaesthetic OR I/V injection

S/S

-Light headedness, sedation, circumoral paresthesia, twitching, seizures.

Severe toxicity: S/S sudden loss of consciousness with or without consciousness or Cardiovascular compromises with arrythmia.

Treatment:

382.Stop injection still not stable
383.Lipid Rescue
-Bolus = 1.5mg/kg Repeat Bolus

Over 1min (max [3])

-Infusion 15mg/kg/hr (5 min apart) + Double infusion 30m/kg/hr (5 min apart).
384.Intra lipid 20% should be available
385.All cases reported to NHS

Mechanism of action:

386.Lipid sink
387.Inhibit L/A inhibition of myocardial fatty acid oxidation.
⇨Anaphylaxis:

Mast cell tryptase levels – 1-2 hours after anaphylaxis, 3 samples

1 – 3.5/100,000 with 1% mortality.

388.Remove agents
389.ABCDE
390.Adrenaline 1:1000 – 0.5ml => I/M

1:10,000 – 0.5ml => I/V

Adjuvant - Hydrocortisone 20mg. - Chlorpheniramine 10mg.

due to systolic HTN, aneurysm, AVM
